- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to over-forecast (especially after spikes), apply downward correction by 5–15% of forecasted peak.
- After a sharp upward spike in price, model often overshoots and fails to correct — reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 3–5 days if sentiment turns negative.
- If sentiment alternates sharply (e.g., +1, -1, +1), model overreacts to short-term sentiment swings — dampen forecast volatility by smoothing 3-day moving average.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline after peak), model fails to recognize — adjust forecast downward by 3–8% per day of reversion.
- If sentiment history shows high negative sentiment (≥ 3 consecutive -1.00), model tends to over-forecast — apply bias correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast if price is above 85% of recent 7-day high.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates volatility — reduce forecast by 1–3% if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- If true outcome shows sudden drop after model peak, model often fails to anticipate — apply lag correction: reduce forecast by 5–10% if true outcome drops > 5% from model peak within 2 days.
